thread:
maria: Quick sync — sketching a long-term platform roadmap focused on multi-region + multi-tenant isolation. Putting customer asks, launch criteria, and cost tradeoffs together for prioritization. TL;DR: we need a proposed set of isolation tiers, cutover runway, and measurable launch gates by EOW.

alex: +1. do we have a concrete hypothesis on which customers need strict VPC/on-prem vs Dedicated reservations?

tara: From sales: 3 enterprise deals next quarter asking for data-residency + private deployment. They care about SLA (99.9%), audit logs, and predictable latency. They'd accept a 3–6 month cutover window if we provide a migration checklist.

sam: For runtime, isolation impacts batching and cache hit rates — big cost delta. We should model p50/p95 latencies and unit cost per 1M tokens for each tier (hosted / dedicated / private). I can run sims if we define traffic profiles.

jess: Ops note: rolling customers between slices needs graceful KV cache warmup, fallback policies, and automated evict/rehydration steps. We must include an incident rollback path in the launch gates.

maria: Proposal draft (high level):
- Isolation tiers: "shared-hosted" (default), "reserved-dedicated" (committed GPU pools), "private-vpc/onprem" (customer-managed infra).
- Launch gates: performance (p95 < X ms for target latencies), reliability (SLO > 99.9%), security (KMS + audit + SOC controls), migration docs + runbook, and cost model with expected unit economics.

alex: For "X ms" we should tie to customer SLAs by region. Maybe p95 < 400ms for hosted, <200ms for dedicated. Also call out model-variant fallback (quantized fallback if high-load) as an accepted degradation path.

tara: Customers will want concrete cutover runway: staging pilot with 1–2 customers, then 2–4 week incremental waves. Need a sales-facing checklist: expected downtime (none), behavioral changes to app, and expected billing changes.

sam: I ran a quick back-of-envelope: moving a tenant to dedicated with 8x batching disabled and KV isolation increases cost ~3x on average but drops p95 by ~40%. If we provide autoscaling + burst lanes the delta can be 1.5–2x. Will produce a 3-scenario spreadsheet.

maria: Decision points we need to resolve in this thread:
1) Acceptance criteria for "private" launch (audit, infra packaging, compliance checklist)
2) Tenant migration model (lift+shift vs staged traffic mirroring)
3) Fallback policy defaults (which model variants allowed, regional fallbacks)
4) Pricing signal and committed discount bands for Dedicated

jess: Ops acceptance criteria (draft):
- Canary with synthetic traffic showing no regression for 72h
- Automated rollback if error rate spikes > 2x baseline for 15m
- Runbooks for cache warmup and traffic split
- Telemetry: token-level cost, p50/p95 per-tenant, KV hit ratio

alex: On (2) migration model: prefer staged traffic mirroring for safety. Canary-only is too risky for big customers. We'll need a traffic splitter that supports percentage rollouts at connection-level affinity. Adds infra work but safer.

tara: Sales ask: include a templated customer runbook and an executive slide that explains risk/reward. We can help coordinate pilots if Eng provides an onboarding checklist.

maria: I've put a first-pass acceptance checklist into the roadmap doc (link: https://internal.redwood/inference/roadmap/isolation-econ — please review). Next steps:
- sam: spreadsheet w/ cost scenarios by Tue
- alex: migration API + traffic splitter spec by Wed
- jess: ops canary + rollback SLOs + runbook draft by Wed
- tara: create sales-facing cutover checklist + pilot outreach doc by Thu

deploy-bot: Deploy scheduled — roadmap doc updated (version 2) by maria at 1795559900 :white_check_mark:

alex: One more ask: we should quantify quality regressions for fallback model variants. Ops+Research should add eval prompts to ensure no silent regression.

maria: Agree. Add a gate: "no unapproved intrinsic quality regression on core prompts (by prod-research)". I'll add to the checklist.

tara: I can line up 2 pilot customers who are flexible on timeline but need the compliance checklist. Will share names in DM.

sam: Will post the simulation sheet once done. If we see >2x cost, recommend a dedicated discount tier or gradual throttle to reduce sticker shock.

jess: Flag: SLA reporting needs daily ingestion and an alert-to-owner mapping — otherwise we can't meet enterprise reporting reqs. Ops will need a small dedicated runbook maintainer.

maria: Great feedback — I'll synthesize these action items into a one-pager and slot this initiative into Q3 roadmap prioritization. If anyone has objections to the acceptance gates above, speak now. Otherwise I'll lock the checklist Friday EOD. :eyes:
